name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,465

clue.text: Easy to accomplish data collection without Bill

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the collection wraps around the bill

blocks.note: a file is a collection of data
AC, short for account, which is a bill

explanation.surface: Gathering data turns out simple once Bill is not involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'minus', but here it means outside: F(AC)ILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Facile describes a task achieved with little effort, so it is easily done.

clue.text: Well-known storyteller supporting female friend in Paris

indicators.note: in a down entry, the part supporting sits below the rest

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for female
ami is French for friend
a liar tells stories

explanation.surface: A famous novelist backing a French girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: Storyteller is a crossword stock for LIAR, someone telling tall stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Familiar means commonly recognised or known from frequent experience.

clue.text: Firmly established after study of artist

indicators.note: after places the first-named part later in the answer

blocks.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
stable means secure and fixed

explanation.surface: A painter's reputation became secure after scholars examined him.
explanation.walkthrough: John Constable was the English landscape painter of The Hay Wain.
explanation.definitionFit: Constable is a famous English landscape painter, so an example of a painter.

clue.text: Animal product causing some vascular disease

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used

blocks.note: the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A fatty food blamed for clogged arteries.
explanation.definitionFit: Lard is pig fat rendered for cooking, so it comes from an animal.

clue.text: Pages Hamlet distributed providing a source of information

indicators.note: things distributed are scattered about, so the letters are spread into a new order

blocks.note: PP is the standard abbreviation for pages
taken as written

explanation.surface: Copies of Shakespeare's play handed out to inform people.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet looks like the play being distributed, but its letters join PP and are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A pamphlet is a small leaflet or booklet handed out to tell readers about something.

clue.text: For Joy it's misery not coming back to split even the smallest amount with Miles

indicators.note: coming back means travelling the other way, so the word is read backwards
splitting something means going into its middle

blocks.note: any as in not any at all
taken as written
M is the abbreviation for miles

explanation.surface: Joy finds it miserable not to come home and share even a little with Miles.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole phrase: misery is the opposite of joy, so for that word it is an antonym. Joy and Miles look like people, but only Miles gives letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An antonym is a word of opposite meaning, and misery stands opposite joy in sense.

clue.text: Opportunity after a long time to break through with a thriller perhaps

indicators.note: after sends the opportunity second, behind the long time
breaking into something means entering its middle

blocks.note: per means by way of or through
an age is a very long time
your turn is your chance

explanation.surface: A long-awaited chance to break through with a gripping story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break through' reads as one phrase, but through is a word for by way of, which gets broken open.
explanation.definitionFit: A page-turner is a compelling book you cannot put down, and thrillers are typical examples.

clue.text: Latin name of river insect

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for Latin
the Ouse is a river in England

explanation.surface: Asking for the scientific name of a water bug.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is the name of several English rivers, including one through York.
explanation.definitionFit: A louse is a small wingless parasitic bug that lives on animals and humans.

clue.text: Clement Attlee's content to gossip

indicators.note: the content of the words is what lies inside them

blocks.note: the last letter of the first name and most of the surname

explanation.surface: The postwar Prime Minister happily chatting about others.
explanation.walkthrough: Clement Attlee was Britain's Labour Prime Minister from 1945 to 1951.
explanation.definitionFit: To tattle is to chatter idly or tell tales about other people's affairs.

clue.text: Primitive canoe discovered after search

blocks.note: first meaning: a boat made from a hollowed tree trunk
second meaning: retrieved by digging or rummaging

explanation.surface: An ancient boat found by archaeologists.
explanation.definitionFit: A dugout is a canoe hollowed from a log, and dug out also means unearthed after hunting.

clue.text: Set close to smaller diamonds for example

blocks.note: minor means lesser or smaller
a suit is a set, as of clothes or cards

explanation.surface: Arranging small diamonds next to one another, as a jeweller might.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, clubs and diamonds rank below hearts and spades, so they are the minor suits.
explanation.definitionFit: Diamonds is one of the two lower-ranking card suits in bridge, an example of the category.

clue.text: Haggard's German relative

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for German
an aunt is a family relative

explanation.surface: A worn-out looking member of a German family.
explanation.walkthrough: Haggard reads like the novelist Rider Haggard, but here it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaunt describes a thin, worn and drawn face, just as haggard does.

clue.text: Fools caught out in great numbers

indicators.note: out means removed, so the letter for caught is dropped

blocks.note: clots are stupid people
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Idiots being dismissed by the dozen, as in a cricket collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: CLOTS loses its C to leave LOTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Lots is an informal word for a large quantity or many of something.

clue.text: Having lost some support over tenor being shabby in appearance

indicators.note: lying over the gap, so the tenor is set into the phrase before it

blocks.note: a shoe that is down a heel has lost part of what holds you up
T is the abbreviation for tenor

explanation.surface: A singer whose clothes and fortunes have both worn down.
explanation.walkthrough: DOWN A HEEL takes T in the middle to make DOWN-AT-HEEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Down-at-heel describes someone looking shabby and poor, like a person in worn-out shoes.

clue.text: It's served with a piece of toast at county town dance

indicators.note: a piece of a word here is just its first letter

blocks.note: first letter of the word
Ennis is the county town of County Clare in Ireland
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Something served with toast at a dance in a provincial town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Served' suggests food; the definition is a ball served in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: A player serves the tennis ball to begin each point of a game.

clue.text: Doctor involved in first class hospital department, creating a relaxing atmosphere

indicators.note: something involved in another is caught up inside it

blocks.note: A1 means first-rate, with the digit 1 read as I
MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A doctor working in a top hospital unit keeps the ward calm.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 means first-class, with the digit 1 standing in for the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambient music or lighting is soft background designed to set a calm mood in a space.

clue.text: Bad-tempered sailor on board again

indicators.note: being on board a vessel means being held within it

blocks.note: more means an additional time
OS is an ordinary seaman

explanation.surface: A grumpy seaman who has had to return to his ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board again' reads as returning to the ship, but on board means inside the word for again.
explanation.definitionFit: Morose means sullen and gloomy, so grumpy and ill-humoured in manner.

clue.text: Something foul made palatable with sugar?

definitions.text: Something foul made palatable with sugar?

blocks.clueFragment: Something foul made palatable with sugar?
blocks.note: surface reading: unpleasant food sweetened to make it edible

blocks.clueFragment: Something foul made palatable with sugar?
blocks.note: setter's reading: rude language softened by saying 'sugar!' in its place

explanation.surface: Sweetening nasty medicine so it goes down easily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sugar!' is a polite exclamation people use in place of a ruder expletive.
explanation.definitionFit: Foul language means obscenities, and saying sugar is a mild substitute for one.

clue.text: Spiritual healer embarrassed by Keats regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, taking every other letter
someone embarrassed is thrown into confusion, so the letters are muddled

blocks.note: second and fourth letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: A faith healer flustered by the Romantic poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal means heavenly or otherworldly, so belonging to the realm of the spirit.

clue.text: The central part of town mostly inhabited by sailors

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of the town goes
a place inhabited by people has them living inside it

blocks.note: Keele, a university town in Staffordshire, without its last letter
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: The heart of a naval town, full of sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: Keele is a small university town in Staffordshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A kernel is the core or essential centre of something, like the seed inside a nut.

clue.text: Contact between groups with back trouble is working

indicators.note: back means the word for trouble runs the other way

blocks.note: to ail is to trouble
taken as written
on means operating

explanation.surface: A colleague with a bad back still showing up to work between meetings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back trouble' reads as a sore back, but back reverses trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is communication or cooperation between separate organisations or units.

clue.text: Prince moved to rapture after conclusion of ice show

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: PR is an abbreviation for prince
last letter of the word
sent means thrilled or carried away

explanation.surface: A royal thrilled by a skating spectacle.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an ice show; 'show' is the definition, as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To present something is to display or put it on show for others.

clue.text: Stop over with group of Cubs

blocks.note: Cub Scouts are organised in a pack
up means finished, as in time is up

explanation.surface: A scout leader breaking a journey with the youngsters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop over' looks like one phrase, but over gives UP.
explanation.definitionFit: To pack up means to cease working or to finish, as an engine or a person might.

clue.text: Stomach turned by lines from 'Remember the Alamo' for instance

indicators.note: something turned round faces the opposite way

blocks.note: the craw is a crop or stomach
RY is short for railway lines

explanation.surface: Feeling queasy at a famous line from a Texas battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remember the Alamo' was the rallying cry of Texan troops in 1836.
explanation.definitionFit: A battle slogan shouted to rally soldiers is the very thing this answer names.

clue.text: Support point of view taken on animal insurance at the outset

indicators.note: the outset of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: an ass is a donkey
first letter of the word
a stance is an attitude or position

explanation.surface: Backing an opinion on pet insurance from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Assistance is help or backing given to someone, the noun sense of support.

clue.text: His changes to the Bible upset God

indicators.note: His changes means that word is altered in arrangement
in a down light, upset means turned upside down

blocks.note: taken as written
AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone's revisions of scripture offend a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: Shiva is one of the principal Hindu deities.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiva is a major Hindu deity, the destroyer in the divine trinity.

clue.text: Language coming from Scorsese oddly ignored

indicators.note: ignoring the odd-placed letters leaves only the even ones

blocks.note: second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A film director's strange speech being disregarded.
explanation.walkthrough: Cree is a Native American language spoken in Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: Cree is an Algonquian tongue spoken by First Nations people across Canada.

clue.text: Australian paramilitary movement sent up in song

indicators.note: in a down light, sent up means read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: A is an abbreviation for Australian
the Irish Republican Army

explanation.surface: An Aussie militia mocked in a satirical number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent up' suggests mockery, but it reverses the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo vocal piece in an opera or oratorio.

clue.text: Porcelain from Switzerland popular with Austria's leader

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: CH is the international code for Switzerland
in means fashionable
first letter of the country's name

explanation.surface: Fine tableware from the Alps, prized by an Austrian chancellor.
explanation.definitionFit: China is fine ceramic ware, the material known as porcelain.

clue.text: Starting point in Queens Road not entirely unfamiliar

indicators.note: not entirely means falling short of the whole, so the last letter is lost
something unfamiliar is strange, so these letters appear in a strange order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Getting lost in an unfamiliar street means beginning again.
explanation.walkthrough: Queens Road drops its final D, then the nine letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Back to square one is an idiom for returning to the beginning of a task.

clue.text: Young horse in yard needing attention shown by Heather

blocks.note: Y is an abbreviation for yard
to give ear is to pay attention
ling is the common heather plant

explanation.surface: A colt in a stable yard getting care from a woman named Heather.
explanation.definitionFit: A yearling is a horse in its second year, between one and two years old.

clue.text: An influence on the Spanish composer

blocks.note: to have a hand in something is to influence it
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A Spanish composer who shaped later music.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface implies the composer is Spanish; 'the Spanish' just gives EL.
explanation.definitionFit: Handel was the German-born Baroque composer of Messiah, who worked in London.
